questions.question: Describe two ways of transferring a development to the packaging board, explain why grain or flute direction matters, and state how cut lines and fold lines are treated when cutting the blank.
questions.expected_answer: Mark out directly on the card with pencil, ruler and set square, measuring every dimension from the development and drawing cut and fold lines lightly; or make a full-size template on thin card, cut it out, trace its outline onto the board and prick through its corners to mark fold lines, which is faster for several blanks. Paperboard folds cleanly along its grain and cracks across it, and corrugated board folds along its flutes, so the development is placed with the main folds along the grain or flutes and flutes vertical in panels that carry stacking loads. Only the cut lines (outer edge, slots, windows, tab corner trims) are cut, against a steel ruler on a mat in light passes away from the body; fold lines are never cut but left for scoring.

questions.question: Explain what scoring is and why it is needed, state which side of the fold is scored, and give the correct order for folding and gluing a carton.
questions.expected_answer: Scoring is pressing a blunt tool (bone folder, back of a butter knife, empty ballpoint, scoring wheel) firmly along a ruler on the fold line to crush the fibres without cutting, so the card bends crisply on that line instead of bowing and cracking its surface; thick corrugated board may be half-cut through the top liner or have its flutes crushed. The score is made on the outside of the fold, so the card folds away from the score. Order: score all folds while flat; bend each fold to 90 degrees and back to set it; wrap the side panels into a tube, fold the glue tab inside, hold the tube square and glue the tab with a thin even layer, holding under pressure until it grabs; then fold and glue the base flaps; close the lid last after the product is inside.

questions.question: Describe how a finished package is tested against its functions and how its construction is checked, giving the likely cause of three common faults and two environmental questions to ask.
questions.expected_answer: With the real product inside: protection by shaking, a short drop and stacking weight on it; containment by checking nothing falls out or leaks; information by checking space and legibility for name, contents and date; convenience by opening, closing and carrying; promotion by checking it looks as designed and the window shows the product. Construction: folds crisp and on their lines, box square with equal diagonals, lid closes without forcing, seams hold when pulled, no glue or cut marks outside, size as specified. Faults: a skew box from gluing the base before the tube was square; a cracked fold from scoring on the inside or folding across the grain; a lid that will not tuck from a slot cut too short. Environmental questions: could less material or thinner card have done the job; is the package a single recyclable material or did a film window, coating or glue spoil its recyclability; could recycled board have been used.
